conditions.title: Invalid configuration fails at boot, not at first request
conditions.detail: Boot-time validation is wired; staging/production refuse to serve with invalid config.

conditions.title: Every required secret is present and not trivially weak
conditions.detail: Weak or missing: ADMIN_KEY, AFFILIATE_REDIRECT_SECRET, ANALYTICS_SIGNING_SECRET, CRON_SECRET, DIAGNOSTICS_SECRET. These are read by signed redirects, admin auth, cron access and diagnostics — a weak value is an open door.

conditions.title: SITE_URL is a real HTTPS origin, not a placeholder or localhost
conditions.detail: SITE_URL is currently http://localhost:3000, which cannot serve production. This is a configuration input, not a code defect — nothing in the repo can satisfy it.

blocker.unblockedWhen: SITE_URL is set to the live origin in the deployment environment

conditions.title: Every major product flow is either enabled or deliberately dark
conditions.detail:
2 major flow(s) would be dark at launch:
      - postbackIngestionEnabled=false → affiliate postback ingestion — conversion tracking
      - operatorApprovalEnabled=false → Builder approval and the entire Acca publication chain
      Each must be an explicit decision before launch, not a default.
conditions.evidence: getFeatureFlags() resolved for the target environment (lib/config/featureFlags.ts)
conditions.limitation: This condition proves the flags were LOOKED AT, not that the chosen values are right. That decision is the owner's.

conditions.title: An unparseable flag value falls back to the conservative default
conditions.detail: Unknown values resolve to the conservative fallback rather than enabling a flow by accident.
conditions.evidence: parseBool in lib/config/featureFlags.ts; covered by executed tests

conditions.title: The memory-only durability limits are documented and warned at boot
conditions.detail: The limitation is surfaced at boot. It is a documented constraint, not a solved problem.
conditions.limitation: HTTP idempotency and rate limiting are process-local and do NOT survive a restart or coordinate across instances. Cross-process correctness rests on expectedVersion optimistic concurrency in the persistence layer, not on replay caching.

conditions.title: The deployment runs one instance, or accepts per-instance limits
conditions.detail: Instance count is 1; memory-only limiters are coherent.
conditions.evidence: WEB_CONCURRENCY / PM2_INSTANCES as observed in the environment

conditions.title: The PostgreSQL adapter's SQL structure is verified
conditions.detail: The adapter's statements, columns and guards match the contract, by executed tests.
conditions.limitation: Structural verification reads the SQL. It proves shape, not behaviour: no statement in this adapter has ever been executed against a server.

conditions.title: The PostgreSQL adapter has been exercised against a real server
conditions.detail: NOT EXECUTED. Migrations, constraints, transaction semantics and concurrent conversion behaviour are all unproven. This is the single largest unknown before launch.
conditions.evidence: Requires an executed connection. Structural tests deliberately do NOT satisfy this.

blocker.unblockedWhen: a real DATABASE_URL is reachable and the adapter suite runs against it with exit code 0

conditions.title: A full production build completes with exit code 0
conditions.detail: NOT EXECUTED. The prepare-dev guard correctly refuses to build against a localhost SITE_URL. A localhost build is not a substitute and must not be recorded as one.
conditions.evidence: npm run build against a real HTTPS SITE_URL

blocker.unblockedWhen: SITE_URL is a live HTTPS origin and npm run build exits 0

conditions.title: Release tooling present: build-verify.mjs
conditions.detail: build-verify.mjs is present.

conditions.title: Release tooling present: smoke-staging.mjs
conditions.detail: smoke-staging.mjs is present.

conditions.title: Release tooling present: backup-postgres.mjs
conditions.detail: backup-postgres.mjs is present.

conditions.title: Release tooling present: restore-rehearsal.mjs
conditions.detail: restore-rehearsal.mjs is present.

conditions.title: Release tooling present: rehearse-migrations.mjs
conditions.detail: rehearse-migrations.mjs is present.

conditions.title: Release tooling present: rollback-release.sh
conditions.detail: rollback-release.sh is present.

conditions.title: Staging smoke tests pass against a deployed staging origin
conditions.detail: NOT EXECUTED. No staging environment exists and starting one is out of scope.

conditions.title: Postback requests are authenticated before they are processed
conditions.detail: Incoming postbacks are verified before any conversion is recorded.

conditions.title: The postback IP allowlist is configured
conditions.detail: Not configured. The addresses are supplied by each affiliate network and cannot be invented here.

blocker.requires: the network origins each affiliate network posts from
blocker.unblockedWhen: AFFILIATE_POSTBACK_IP_ALLOWLIST lists those origins in the deployment

conditions.title: Postback ingestion is enabled, so conversions are actually recorded
conditions.detail: postbackIngestionEnabled resolves FALSE in production. Affiliate revenue would be unattributable at launch: clicks would go out and conversions would come back to a closed door. This is the single highest-value flag decision before shipping.
conditions.limitation: Enabling ingestion records conversions. It does not retroactively recover any that arrived while the flag was off — those are lost, not queued.

conditions.title: robots.txt is served
conditions.detail: robots.txt is generated by the app.

conditions.title: Non-production environments are held out of the index
conditions.detail: Staging can be excluded from indexing.
conditions.evidence: STAGING_NOINDEX honoured in app/robots.ts and app/layout.tsx

conditions.title: A sitemap is generated
conditions.detail: A sitemap route exists.
conditions.limitation: Presence is verified here. Whether every intended URL is included, and whether the shard count is right, is only observable against a real build.

conditions.title: Canonical and hreflang come from a single source
conditions.detail: Canonical and hreflang are emitted from one helper, so they cannot drift apart.
conditions.evidence: alternatesFor (lib/seo.ts), built on the resolved site origin
conditions.limitation: Canonical URLs are derived from SITE_URL. While SITE_URL is localhost every canonical the app emits is a localhost URL — correct by construction, wrong in production until the real origin is set.

conditions.title: JSON-LD structured data is emitted
conditions.detail: Structured data modules are present.
conditions.limitation: Emission is verified. Validity against Google's parsers is not — that requires the Rich Results test against live URLs.

conditions.title: The production property is verified in Search Console
conditions.detail: No verification token is configured. Verification cannot precede owning the domain, so this necessarily follows the HTTPS item. Without it there is no index coverage data, no query data and no way to submit the sitemap.
conditions.evidence: A verification token served from the production origin

blocker.requires: ownership of the production domain and a Search Console property
blocker.unblockedWhen: the verification token is configured and Google confirms ownership

conditions.title: An analytics measurement id is configured
conditions.detail: Not configured. Launching without it means the first traffic is unmeasured and unrecoverable — there is no backfill for sessions nobody recorded.

blocker.requires: an analytics property for the production domain
blocker.unblockedWhen: NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID is set in the production environment

conditions.title: Errors are logged structurally, including unhandled ones
conditions.detail: Structured logging is wired and process-level failures are captured.
conditions.evidence: lib/monitoring/logger.ts; unhandledRejection and uncaughtException handlers registered in instrumentation.ts

conditions.title: A health endpoint is served for uptime checks
conditions.detail: A health endpoint is available for an external monitor to poll.
conditions.limitation: The endpoint exists. Nothing is polling it — external uptime monitoring is a deployment concern and is not satisfied by this condition.

conditions.title: A backup has been taken and restored from
conditions.detail: NOT EXECUTED. The scripts exist, which is not the same as a backup that has been proven to restore. An untested backup is an assumption, not a safety net.

blocker.unblockedWhen: a backup is taken and a restore rehearsal completes with exit code 0

conditions.title: A rollback has been rehearsed against a real deployment
conditions.detail: NOT EXECUTED. Script presence is already covered separately; this item is about having run it. The first rollback should not happen during the first incident.

blocker.requires: a deployed environment to roll back
blocker.unblockedWhen: a rollback rehearsal completes against staging with exit code 0

[external] a reachable PostgreSQL server → a real DATABASE_URL is reachable and the adapter suite runs against it with exit code 0
[external] a real production HTTPS domain → SITE_URL is a live HTTPS origin and npm run build exits 0

[external] the network origins each affiliate network posts from → AFFILIATE_POSTBACK_IP_ALLOWLIST lists those origins in the deployment

[external] an analytics property for the production domain → NEXT_PUBLIC_GTM_ID is set in the production environment
[external] a reachable PostgreSQL server → a backup is taken and a restore rehearsal completes with exit code 0
[external] a deployed environment to roll back → a rollback rehearsal completes against staging with exit code 0
[repo] Every required secret is present and not trivially weak
[repo] Every major product flow is either enabled or deliberately dark
[repo] Postback ingestion is enabled, so conversions are actually recorded
